## 1. What this block is, in one sentence

**This is the volume's resolution block and its title is *The Mapped Scar*, and it is the only block in the whole volume in which the Many-Handed is crossed and the volume's one System panel is spent.** A flare on the mapped ground, ten routes held at once, the Wound mapped and contained and **not erased**, the origin answered, and a resolution that is negative and local: **the question of who should hold the Gatehouse is now the question, and it is worse than the question this volume opened with, and nobody in nine counties is going to be told that either.**

## 3. The block's frame, derived and not copied

**The single anchor is day 2310, the twenty-fifth of Goatmonth YR 321, a Monday**, which is the last page of Volume 14 and is stated four times in that volume's close record. **Block 0005 is days 2551 to 2610 inclusive, sixty days, and every day of it is YR 322, and it is the LAST BLOCK OF THE VOLUME.** **Wolfmonth the first is day 2556, which is a TUESDAY, and is NOT a market morning, and Frostmonth the first is day 2586, which is a THURSDAY, and IS a market morning, and Hearthmonth the first is day 2616, which is outside this volume, and the volume ends on the twenty-fifth of Frostmonth at day 2610, which is a SUNDAY and is NOT a market morning.** **THE BLOCK THEREFORE CARRIES ONE MONTH BOUNDARY AND NOT TWO, at day 2556, and no day of it is in Fallowmonth, and no day of it is in Thawmonth, Mudmonth, Longlight, Rainmonth, Harvestmonth or Goatmonth.**

**Market mornings are the Saturdays and the Thursdays**, and **the market mornings inside this block's sixty days are EIGHTEEN of them, being days 2551, 2553, 2558, 2560, 2565, 2567, 2572, 2574, 2579, 2581, 2586, 2588, 2593, 2595, 2600, 2602, 2607 and 2609, and the last of them is 2609, which is a Saturday and one day short of the volume's last day, which is itself a Sunday and is not a market morning.** **DAY 2551 IS ITSELF A THURSDAY AND IS A MARKET MORNING, so the block's first day can carry a market-morning dateline, which none of the four blocks before it could.** The house pattern of this volume's four blocks has been a cluster early, a spread, and the last chapter on the block's last day or near it. **Write the ten datelines down before you write the first chapter and reconcile every one of them against the chain, because a successor inherits them.**

**A writer derives the day of month and the weekday separately from the day number and never copies a row out of the printed table at `outline/volume-13.md` §17, which is wrong in five rows and is a certificate and not an authority.** **The ten days of this block, which the writer chooses and which must then be printed in the dateline and must reconcile on the chain: five market mornings and five not, spread across the sixty days, with the last of them on or near day 2610.** **A chapter may not be dated in days 2556 to 2585 and print a day of month above thirty, and the same rule holds for days 2586 to 2615 inside Frostmonth.**

## 4. What the block must contain

**THE MANY-HANDED, CROSSED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE, AND IT IS CROSSED WHILE ASKING AND THE ASKING IS WHAT MAKES IT COST.** `outline/volume-15.md` §4 states that Stage 6, the Many-Handed, is crossed in Block 0005 and not before. **No chapter of Blocks 0001 to 0004 crossed it and no chapter of any of them printed a System panel, and this is the block that spends the volume's one panel and it may spend ONE.** **The volume's other cost is that he can no longer be near the works without asking somebody to stand with him, and that cost is real and it is on the page and it is not cured inside these ten chapters.**

**THE WOUND IS MAPPED AND CONTAINED AND NOT ERASED.** `outline/volume-15.md` §10 item 2 is binding: **it is a visible scar that about nine people in nine counties can now point at on a map, in the same shape as the exposed wall in Volume 14 and worse for everybody. NO CHAPTER SAYS IT IS CURED AND NO CHAPTER SAYS IT IS SMALL.** **Do not erase it, do not heal it, and do not call it closed.**

**THE ORIGIN IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWERING DOES NOT INCLUDE A REUNION AND DOES NOT INCLUDE ANYBODY'S BODY.** `outline/volume-15.md` §10 item 1. **What is found in this block is NOT a set of notes.** `outline/volume-15.md` §14 and `state/open-threads.md` 648 record that **Ilyra Kest's route notes are not produced, not quoted, not mentioned and not known to exist in Blocks 0001 to 0004, and in Block 0005 what is found is a BOUNDARY AND A REFUSAL.** A successor may not print the notes, may not mention them, and may not know that they exist.

**THE RESOLUTION IS NEGATIVE AND LOCAL, AND IT IS THE VOLUME'S POINT.** `outline/volume-15.md` §8 Block 5 and §10 item 3: **both paths refused him and he accepted it, and the acceptance is permanent and is NOT ARGUED WITH IN THIS BLOCK.** The two refusals were given on the fourteenth and the twenty-sixth of Fallowmonth and are recorded in full at `state/continuity.md` 1668 and `state/open-threads.md` 662. **A chapter of this block may not reopen either of them, may not have anybody ask either of those two men anything again, may not have the man of thirty-two want either of them again, and may not print a softer version of either refusal.** `state/open-threads.md` 664 adds the fourth wall: **nobody looks over the ninth of the nine stones from this side, because the volume has ruled that out on the page, and a successor may not treat that omission as an oversight and may not show the far side of them as though it had been earned.**

**THE QUESTION NOBODY CAN HOLD IS THE BLOCK'S ORDINARY BACKGROUND AND NOT ITS FINDING:** a finding that is in four hundred mouths and in nobody's hand, in a county that cannot call a meeting, cannot reach a hearing, and has nine clerks it cannot put a thing in front of. **What is new in this block is not the finding and not the county. What is new is that the map exists.** About nine people in nine counties can point at a thing on a map. About nine hundred yards of an old road is still in about four hundred mouths and still in nobody's hand, and that is now a separate thing from the scar, and the block's job is to keep it separate.

**THE ORDINARY HALF, AND IT IS LONG AND IT IS NOT DECORATIVE.** Eight of nine yards of the wall back in and a last yard not started, and one man carrying stone two miles in his own hands since the second of Mudmonth, which is two hundred and four days on the first day of this block and two hundred and sixty-three on its last. A drove of nine beasts on every Thursday since the second of Mudmonth, which is thirty drove on the first day of this block, thirty-five by the first of Frostmonth and thirty-eight by the twenty-fifth, and nobody goes with it. Brood frames that stood at five on the twenty-fifth of Embermonth and come back in about four weeks, and a young man who said out loud he is not going to make more bees than the bees he has got. **About nine acres of broom on that east rise that was cut on the fourth of Rainmonth and had about nine days of it left to be cut that year, and in this block the broom is off the hill again and about nine days of it is cut and about nine hundred yards of it is left standing, and a line in grass that is not cut closes over in about three years.** The hives, the walled yard, the two miles of wall and orchard between the eleventh mile stone and the top of that hill. The weigh-house and about four hundred and nine parish rolls a month and Frostmonth being a month they come past in. The market street on a Saturday. The room over the weigh-house. **Nine households that cut a road's grass for a boundary and not for a road, and the rota of beasts kept about nine years, and the fact that no third household came up and nobody asked it for a reason.**

## 5. The ending of the block and the ending of the volume

**A completed beat, and the volume's resolution, which is negative.** The scar is on a map and about nine people can point at it. The origin is answered and the answer contains no body and no reunion. The acceptance of the two refusals stands and is not argued with. **And the question the volume ends on is who should hold the Gatehouse, and it is worse than the question the volume opened with, and nobody in nine counties is going to be told that either.**

**`outline/volume-15.md` §11 and `outline/series.md` set up three things for Volume 16 and this volume must set up all three in its own terms and in its own last pages:** a path that closes itself for its own reasons; a Gatehouse that is now mapped rather than hidden; **and a request from the road office four hundred miles off that this county cannot answer and that it has been unable to answer since the first of Goatmonth YR 321.** `state/open-threads.md` 630 forbids tracing who asked the fen county road office for the roll and that stays forbidden; **a request FROM the road office is a different thing and is not forbidden, and it is the third of the three things and it is the shape of the hand-off.**

**`outline/volume-15.md` §10 item 5 is binding and is the volume's relationship work:** **Aren Kest and the woman of about twenty-nine who keeps the room are FURTHER APART at the close of this volume than at the close of Volume 14, and each of them has built one thing that does not depend on the other.** **The separation is not mended in this block. No exchange of words between them in any of the ten files. Nothing between them in any document. They may be in one room with a third person in it and may not be alone in one. The four and a half years are never described as four and a half years about the two of them.**

**AND THE VOLUME-CLOSE RECORD.** **Because this is the fifth block of five, a successor should write the volume's close record as part of its own phase, at `outline/volumes/volume-15-close.md`, and NOT as a sixth batch.** Thirteen of the fourteen closed volumes have one and Volume 10 does not, and that gap is a records gap and is recorded rather than filled at `state/open-threads.md` 539. **A phase that closes a volume writes the close record for the volume it has just closed and does not create another phase.**

## 7. The house prose, and the four mechanical rules that are not taste

**The voice is in Chapters 0738 and 0740, and in 0733 and 0735.** Read them before writing a sentence and match them: short declaratives, a flat cadence, a great many plain negatives, the census sentence where who-understood is the point, and physical work, weather and distance everywhere else.

1. **Zero em dashes, zero en dashes, zero semicolons, zero exclamation marks, zero single asterisks and therefore no italics, zero straight double quotes and zero curly apostrophes.** Speech takes curly doubles. Apostrophes are straight. Per-line bold parity even on every line. Every file ends in a newline.
2. **One footed money column per chapter**: ten items, priced 1 to 41, a mark at forty-eight pence in every conversion, and the coda that names the figures in the chapter that are not in it. **THE CEILING IS 343 PENCE AND IT IS ARITHMETIC: with ten distinct prices drawn from 1 to 41 with the barred six, 14, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41, excluded, the ten largest available are 40, 39, 37, 36, 35, 34, 32, 31, 30 and 29, and they sum to 343.** **The barred numerals may not be a price, an over-figure or a printed total anywhere.** Foot the column four ways and check the conversion separately from the sum. **A successor needs a tenth distinct total and cannot find one should read `state/continuity.md` item 1674 before it changes a price band, and that item is the binding one.** **THE COLLISION SET OVER SEVEN HUNDRED AND THIRTY PRIOR FILES LEAVES SIX USABLE FREE VALUES: 136, 166, 232, 236, 332 AND 336, AND OF THOSE 136 IS ALREADY SPENT BY BATCH 0004, WHICH LEAVES FIVE, WHICH IS NOT TEN. A BLOCK NEEDS TEN COLUMNS.** **The route that works and that Batch 0004 took is BELOW SIXTY: five distinct totals below sixty are arithmetically reachable with ten distinct non-barred prices, being 55, 56, 57, 58 and 59, and a sixth is not, because ten distinct non-barred prices cannot sum below fifty-five.** **SO A SUCCESSOR MUST TAKE BOTH ROUTES, AND SAID SO ON THE PAGE IN ITS OWN RECORDS: five columns below sixty and five from the six usable free values, five of which are 166, 232, 236, 332 and 336.** **Ten collision-free totals cannot be written in the band sixty to three hundred and forty-three by any block, and a successor looking for a better set is looking for something that does not exist, and the collision paragraph at `state/continuity.md` 1649 which says twenty-two and prints twenty-one is the standing proof of that.**
3. **`about` density.** Volume 15 Batch 0004 ran 23.30 to 26.83 per 1,000 with no page at or above 28.00, and the three blocks before it ran 22.26 to 27.70, 21.32 to 29.49 and 24.99 to 26.59. **Aim for 22 to 27 and no page at or above 28.00. Keep the census sentence for the two or three beats in a chapter where who understood is the point and write the rest as action, weather or silence.** Chapter length: Batch 0004 ran at a mean of 3,306 and its minimum chapter is 3,078. **Do not write below 3,000.** **AND THE CRAFT ADVICE AT `state/open-threads.md` 647, WHICH THE LAST BLOCK TOOK AND WHICH THE BLOCK BEFORE IT PRODUCED: hold the census-opener share at or under seventy-five per cent of prose paragraphs. Batch 0003 ran at 89.6 per cent and read as liturgy on about a third of its pages, and Batch 0004 ran at 70.5 per cent, being 260 of 369, and the only change was that the ordinary half of a day was written as work, weather, distance and silence.** A block that needs to be shorter should do that and not cut the census out of the beats that need it.
4. **Every count attached to a printed speech is footed off the printed words beside it**, and where a claim cannot be counted off the words printed next to it, the claim is cut rather than left wrong. **A printed speech that has a word count beside it must have its words printed, and an unprinted speech must have no count.** This is the single most repeated finding in this manuscript's reviews, and it is what a System panel is most likely to break: **if the panel carries a number, that number is a printed figure and it must foot.**
